drhp.business: The Company manufactures and supplies cast polypropylene (CPP) and cast polyethylene (CPE) films tailored to the needs of the flexible packaging industry and high-end thermoforming applications. Its portfolio spans high-clarity films for premium packaging through to high-barrier films for extended shelf life, serving customers across food and beverage, clothing, flowers and other consumer goods. Management describes the core business as manufacturing flexible and rigid packaging films, driven by innovation, sustainability and customer satisfaction, with a stated focus on value-added products …
drhp.end_markets: Food and beverage (snacks, bakery products, frozen foods, confectionery)|Clothing|Flowers|Other consumer goods|Flexible packaging converters|High-end thermoforming applications|Domestic and international markets (the Company reported foreign exchange earned of Rs. 2,113.33 lakh during the year)
drhp.expansion: The annual report contains no named expansion project, commissioning timeline or capacity-addition programme. The only forward capacity language is the Chairman's stated strategic vision: 'We aim to expand our manufacturing capacity, invest in advanced technologies, and strengthen our presence in both domestic and international markets' — with no project, site, size, cost or date attached. On the existing base, the MD&A states only that the Company is 'presently equipped with such a manufacturing facility capable of producing CPP & CPE films spanning a thickness range from 15 to 250 microns' …
drhp.mdna: Expanding global food and beverage industry is a significant driver of CPP film demand — CPP films increasingly used for snacks, bakery products, frozen foods and confectionery for their superior moisture barrier and heat-sealing properties|Industry emphasis on product freshness, visual appeal and extended shelf life is driving innovation in high-performance CPP films and supporting continued market growth|Indian packaging demand expanding on rapid growth in consumer markets, especially processed food, personal care and pharmaceutical end-users; rising population, income levels and changing …
drhp.one_liner: 3B Films Limited is a Vadodara-based manufacturer and supplier of CPP and CPE films for the flexible packaging industry and high-end thermoforming applications, with a facility capable of producing films spanning 15 to 250 microns.

risks.note: Management attributes the year's decline in revenue and profitability to 'fluctuations in raw material prices' and cites 'elevated raw material prices, volatility in crude oil prices' as a pressure on the packaging industry — polymer input cost is the dominant swing factor for a CPP/CPE film maker with limited pass-through in a weak-demand year
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and crude-oil linkage

risks.note: FY2025-26 is described as 'a challenging operating environment, with pressure on demand ... and global economic uncertainties', with 'subdued demand across certain end-user segments'; revenue from operations fell to Rs 6,001.30 lakhs from Rs 8,530.75 lakhs and the Company witnessed a decline in both revenue and profitability

MD&A Risks & Concerns: 'the chance that competitive forces could prevent the Company from achieving its goal on account of declining revenues or margins' — a commodity-adjacent film business with no disclosed capacity or cost advantage

MD&A names 'logistical, economic, political, cultural, competitive and infrastructural concerns'; mitigation is supplier diversification and a management strategy against disruptions. Higher logistics costs are separately cited by the Chairman as a pressure during the year

A material share of activity is cross-border — foreign exchange earned of Rs 2,113.33 lakh against foreign exchange outgo of Rs 1,584.00 lakh during FY26 — leaving earnings exposed to currency movement and to trade/tariff conditions in export markets; the MD&A itself frames opportunity around US, UAE and UK plastics trade
MD&A flags 'critical skill shortages, increasing staff attrition or significant workforce retirement'; mitigation is training, HR practices and rewards to retain talent

MD&A flags sovereign policy changes that 'adversely impact the financial stability of the Company' and compliance risk carrying 'legal and financial penalties for failing to act under internal and external regulations'; plastics packaging is a directly regulated end-use

Key operating premises sit inside related-party arrangements — a five-year rent agreement with associate 3B Flexipacks Private Limited over the Masar, Padra premises running only to 18.05.2027, and a Hans Export lease whose stated term ended 31.07.2025 — alongside unsecured loans from Babariya-family KMPs, so continuity of premises and funding rests on associate/family entities. A Non-Executive Independent Director (Ms. Mital Devani) also resigned with effect from 30 May 2026
risks.risk: Dependence on related-party premises and concentrated family control

internal_operational.risk: Our company engages in the manufacturing and supply of different types of CPP & CPE films.

The quantity and cost of our products are dependent on our ability to source raw materials at acceptable prices and maintain a stable and sufficient supply of the same.

The products our company consume as raw materials are subject to price volatility and unavailability caused by external conditions, such as commodity price fluctuations within India and globally, weather conditions, supply and demand dynamics, logistics, our bargaining power with the suppliers, inflation and governmental regulations and policies.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management attributes the year's decline in revenue and profitability to 'fluctuations in raw material prices' and cites 'elevated raw material prices, volatility in crude oil prices' as a pressure on the packaging industry — polymer input cost is the dominant swing factor for a CPP/CPE film maker with limited pass-through in a weak-demand year
- FY2025-26 is described as 'a challenging operating environment, with pressure on demand ... and global economic uncertainties', with 'subdued demand across certain end-user segments'; revenue from operations fell to Rs 6,001.30 lakhs from Rs 8,530.75 lakhs and the Company witnessed a decline in both revenue and profitability
- MD&A Risks & Concerns: 'the chance that competitive forces could prevent the Company from achieving its goal on account of declining revenues or margins' — a commodity-adjacent film business with no disclosed capacity or cost advantage
- MD&A names 'logistical, economic, political, cultural, competitive and infrastructural concerns'; mitigation is supplier diversification and a management strategy against disruptions. Higher logistics costs are separately cited by the Chairman as a pressure during the year
- A material share of activity is cross-border — foreign exchange earned of Rs 2,113.33 lakh against foreign exchange outgo of Rs 1,584.00 lakh during FY26 — leaving earnings exposed to currency movement and to trade/tariff conditions in export markets; the MD&A itself frames opportunity around US, UAE and UK plastics trade
- MD&A flags 'critical skill shortages, increasing staff attrition or significant workforce retirement'; mitigation is training, HR practices and rewards to retain talent
- MD&A flags sovereign policy changes that 'adversely impact the financial stability of the Company' and compliance risk carrying 'legal and financial penalties for failing to act under internal and external regulations'; plastics packaging is a directly regulated end-use
- Key operating premises sit inside related-party arrangements — a five-year rent agreement with associate 3B Flexipacks Private Limited over the Masar, Padra premises running only to 18.05.2027, and a Hans Export lease whose stated term ended 31.07.2025 — alongside unsecured loans from Babariya-family KMPs, so continuity of premises and funding rests on associate/family entities. A Non-Executive Independent Director (Ms. Mital Devani) also resigned with effect from 30 May 2026
